Gomoku on NoCharge — why the variant is the contract

NoCharge Gomoku uses a straightforward five-or-more rule on a 15-by-15 board. The current engine has no Renju-style forbidden-move or opening restriction system.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Five in a row, two players, one device.

Play GomokuBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: The current NoCharge Gomoku game is a local two-player contest on a 15-by-15 grid. Players alternate placing one stone on an empty intersection. A continuous horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of five or more wins.

What the V2 rule counts

The line check counts stones extending in both directions from the newly placed stone. Five is enough to win, and a longer line also meets the rule. The current engine does not implement Renju-style forbidden patterns, a restricted first move, captures, or a rule that rejects overlines.

The first player is shown as X in the seeded starting state. The visible move count records placements; it is not a points score. A full board without a winning line is a draw.

Local turn-taking and controls

Both players use the same page and device. Choose an empty intersection directly or set its row and column and activate the placement control. The status identifies the next player. Reset restores the empty starting board and center cursor.

These are the rules in the current Gomoku page, not a survey of every tournament or regional variant. Check that page for the live interface before play.
